checks.note: The auth page lists OAuth access tokens (multi-account apps), static auth tokens, service keys (Bearer), client-credentials tokens (webhooks journal only), and developer API keys (hapikey, specific app features only). It also lists personal access keys for CLI use only. OAuth is for API access by apps installed in multiple accounts, not just login. The 'API key' entry is limited to the developer API key and is not a general API auth method, which the record already says.

The account-types page confirms developer test accounts are free (90-day trial of enterprise features, expire without API calls, renewable) and that standard accounts can be free or paid. It does not say whether a free account has API access, or whether any plan tier is needed. self_serve_free stays as the best-supported value.

The contacts page shows resource-style HTTP endpoints (/crm/v3/objects/contacts) with read, write, batch, upsert, delete and association calls. It also references the Associations, Properties, Search and Engagements APIs. No GraphQL is mentioned. The page never says 'REST' (inferred), and 'broad' is a judgment from the multiple object APIs rather than a stated claim.

HubSpot's own developer docs describe a remote MCP server at https://mcp.hubspot.com, using OAuth with PKCE through an MCP connector. The page does not use the word 'official', but it is vendor-hosted documentation. Some tools need Professional or Enterprise plans.

ready_with_caveats follows from the other fields. The caveats are plan-tier limits on some features, the need to host an OAuth backend for multi-account apps, and unverified free-account API scope. The rate-limit and date-based versioning points were not checked on a fetched page.

corrected.one_liner: HubSpot is a CRM platform with marketing, sales, service, content and commerce hubs, plus a developer platform for building integrations.
corrected.auth_notes: Auth doc lists: OAuth (Bearer access token per installed account, for multi-account/Marketplace apps); static auth (single-account app with a static access token, the successor to private apps); service keys (scoped Bearer keys); client-credentials tokens (webhooks journal API only). Developer API keys (hapikey query param) are not a general API auth method and apply only to certain app features. Personal access keys are for CLI use only.
corrected.access_notes: Developer test accounts are free (90-day trial of many enterprise features; they expire unless API calls are made, and can be renewed). Standard accounts can be free or paid. No fetched page states whether a free standard account has full API access, so that is unconfirmed. Some features need paid hubs (e.g. MCP quotes and AEO tools need Professional/Enterprise; custom pipelines are not on free tools).
corrected.blocker: Plan-tier limits on some features, and a multi-account integration needs an OAuth backend (and a Marketplace listing or limited allowlist for distribution). Rate limits and free-account API scope were not verified. Date-based API versioning requires tracking versions.
